newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ag exports dip 10 pct in Jan from yr ago - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ag exports dip 10 pct in Jan from yr ago - USDA.

text.p: The Agriculture Department Monday said U.S. agricultural exports in January stood at $5 billion, down 10 percent from a year ago, while imports rose to $3 billion, 11 percent above January 1996's level.

USDA said cumulative exports for fiscal 1997, at $21.4 billion, were nearly the same as a year ago. Year-to-date imports were up 14 percent to $11.6 billion, with the European Union and Canada accounting for much of the growth.
USDA said Canada was the largest single-country supplier, with $2.4 billion, a 20 percent rise over 1996, while imports from the EU were $3.5 billion, an eight percent increase.

The department said year-to-date imports of grains and products were $1 billion, up 20 percent from the prior year and that animals and animal products, imported largely from Canada, were up 11 percent from last year's $2.1 billion.
On exports, USDA said January wheat exports tumbled to 1.7 million tonnes versus 2.6 million tonnes in January 1996 and that year-to-date shipments lagged 1996's pace by 33 percent.
Corn exports in January were 4.6 million tonnes, down 15 percent from January 1996. USDA said Japan imported 1.5 million tonnes, up 15 percent from December 1996.

USDA said soybean exports were 2.9 million tonnes in January, unchanged from a year ago. Exports to the EU remained strong in January at 1.5 million tonnes. Year-to-date soybean exports were 13 million tonnes, 33 percent above 1996.

Poultry exports reached $183 million in January, a seven percent gain over the same period in 1996. The volume of beef exports was comparable to January 1996 but value dipped 14 percent due to lower prices, the department said.
